facts.value: Within 30 days after declaring invalidity and proposing a cure, the municipality must make specific findings by resolution and begin preparing and considering a curative amendment.
facts.supporting_quote: Within 30 days following such declaration and proposal ... By resolution make specific findings ... Begin to prepare and consider a curative amendment

facts.value: Within 180 days of the declaration and proposal, the municipality must enact a curative amendment to validate or reaffirm the ordinance under section 609 to cure the declared invalidity.
facts.supporting_quote: Within 180 days from the date of the declaration and proposal, the municipality shall enact a curative amendment

facts.value: On initiation, clause (3) limits requirements to consider specified landowner curative amendments or provide zoning hearing board reports requested after the declaration on identical or substantially similar grounds. It does not state a general stop on permits.
facts.supporting_quote: shall not be required to entertain or consider any landowner's curative amendment ... nor shall the zoning hearing board be required to give a report ... subsequent to the declaration and proposal based upon the grounds identical to or substantially similar

facts.value: Upon completion of clauses (1) and (2), clause (3) limits accrual from the declaration date of specified landowner cure rights based on the invalidity for which a curative amendment was made.
facts.supporting_quote: Upon completion of the procedures as set forth in clauses (1) and (2), no rights to a cure ... shall, from the date of the declaration and proposal, accrue

facts.value: After use of the procedure, the statute generally restricts reuse for 36 months after enactment or reaffirmation, with an exception for a substantially new duty arising from a statutory change or Pennsylvania appellate decision.
facts.supporting_quote: may not again utilize said procedure for a 36-month period ... if ... there is a substantially new duty or obligation ... by virtue of a change in statute or ... a Pennsylvania Appellate Court decision

facts.value: Resolution 21-2026 declared the zoning ordinance substantively invalid in part concerning data center uses and energy generation systems and proposed a curative amendment. It was adopted March 31, 2026.
facts.supporting_quote: substantively invalid in part as it relates to the regulation of data center uses and energy generation systems

facts.value: Resolution 21-2026 directed officials to prepare a separate findings resolution for consideration within 30 days and to prepare a curative amendment.
facts.supporting_quote: begin preparing a resolution for consideration of the Board of Supervisors within thirty (30) days

facts.value: Resolution 25-2026, adopted April 27, 2026, issued specific findings on data center uses and energy generation systems and renewed the direction to prepare a curative amendment.
facts.supporting_quote: the Township Board of Supervisors hereby issues its findings as to the declared invalidity ... as to data centers, energy generation systems

facts.value: The findings said the ordinance did not explicitly define or regulate the uses, that the industrial-district catchall was inadequate, and that existing environmental standards did not adequately address potential impacts.
facts.supporting_quote: The Township Zoning Ordinance does not explicitly define or regulate Data Center Uses or Energy Generation Systems.

facts.value: The signed Ordinance 385-2026 was enacted September 24, 2026 and states that it becomes effective immediately upon adoption.
facts.supporting_quote: This Ordinance shall become effective immediately upon adoption.

facts.value: Ordinance 385-2026 adds data centers subject to section 200-43.1 as a conditional use. Its stated intent is to allow them only in the Industrial Zoning District under strict conditions, not to prohibit them outright.
facts.locator: Page 2, sections I and II, section 200-43.1(1)(B)
facts.supporting_quote: as a Use permitted by Conditional Use ... not to prohibit the use outright

facts.value: The ordinance's savings clause says the amendment does not affect acts, accrued rights, duties, penalties or legal proceedings existing under the zoning code before its effective date.
facts.supporting_quote: shall not affect any act done, any right accrued, any duty imposed, any penalty incurred, or any legal proceeding commenced or pending

facts.value: The repealer reaches ordinances or resolutions directly inconsistent with the ordinance, only to the extent of the inconsistencies.
facts.supporting_quote: directly inconsistent with any provision of this Ordinance are hereby repealed to the extent of such inconsistencies only

uncertainties: Only pages 1, 2, 31 and 32 of the 32-page ordinance are supplied. The omitted provisions may bear on the amendment's scope and its relationship to the municipal cure.
The supplied text does not expressly state that Resolution 21-2026 or 25-2026 terminated on September 24, 2026, or that Ordinance 385-2026 completed this specific municipal cure.

The chronology supports an inference that the recorded process progressed from declaration, to findings, to adoption of related data-center regulations. It does not by itself establish the exact legal endpoint, compliance with every curative procedure, treatment of standalone energy generation, surviving rights, or current force of the resolutions.
The ordinance's inconsistency-only repealer and savings clause do not by themselves establish a blanket repeal of the resolutions or determine which rights accrued or survive.

field_decisions.reason: The ordinance establishes data-center regulations but does not expressly identify itself as completing this cure or replacing either resolution. Its repealer reaches only direct inconsistencies, and the supplied pages do not establish the resolutions’ complete legal status.
September 24 is the ordinance’s adoption and immediate effective date, not an expressly established termination date for the earlier protection.

field_decisions.value: The March 31 declaration initiated the municipal curative-amendment procedure. Section 609.2 requires findings and preparation within 30 days and enactment of a curative amendment within 180 days. The endpoint of the earlier protection is not established by the supplied sources.
field_decisions.reason: The proposed replacement date is not established. The statutory cure deadline is not a blanket permit sunset, and the later ordinance does not expressly terminate the resolutions.

field_decisions.value: Resolution 2026-21 invoked MPC section 609.2, declared partial zoning invalidity concerning data-center uses and energy-generation systems, and proposed a cure. Resolution 25-2026 made specific findings and renewed the direction to prepare a curative amendment. Section 609.2(3) addresses specified curative amendments and reports on identical or substantially similar grounds; it does not itself impose a general permit ban. Ordinance 385-2026 establishes conditional-use data-center zoning, includes a savings clause and an inconsistency-only repealer, and took effect immediately upon its September 24 adoption.
field_decisions.locator: Resolution 2026-21 pages 1–2; Resolution 25-2026 pages 1–2; section 609.2(3); ordinance pages 2, 31–32
field_decisions.reason: The proposed wording attributes invocation to both resolutions. The second resolution instead recites the first invocation, makes findings and renews the preparation direction.

field_decisions.value: Resolution 2026-21 was adopted March 31, 2026, and Resolution 25-2026 supplied findings on April 27. Ordinance 385-2026 was enacted and became effective September 24, establishing data-center regulations. The earlier protection’s endpoint, the ordinance’s relationship to the municipal cure, surviving rights and current applicability remain unresolved.
field_decisions.reason: Labeling replacement an inference does not establish it. The ordinance’s operative relationship to the cure, treatment of standalone energy generation, and effect on earlier resolutions are not established by the supplied pages.

field_decisions.value: The Board enacted Ordinance 385-2026 on September 24, 2026, with immediate effect. It provides for conditional-use data centers and states an intent not to prohibit them outright. Its relationship to completion or replacement of the earlier municipal cure remains unresolved.
field_decisions.reason: Adoption of related data-center regulations does not by itself establish replacement of the entire curative-amendment process or determine surviving effects.
